lines.text: Type two words into a search box: coronavirus origin.
lines.caption: Type two words into a search box: coronavirus origin.

lines.text: Behind it are 171,332 scientific papers.
lines.caption: Behind it are 171,332 scientific papers.

lines.text: Back come ten titles, best first, in about two milliseconds.
lines.caption: Back come ten titles, best first, in about two milliseconds.

lines.text: How?
lines.caption: How?

lines.text: It's two problems.
lines.caption: It's two problems.

lines.text: Find the papers that match, without reading them all.
lines.caption: Find the papers that match, without reading them all.

lines.text: Then put the best ones first.
lines.caption: Then put the best ones first.

lines.text: And a third problem makes it engineering.
lines.caption: And a third problem makes it engineering.

lines.text: When you change something, how do you know the results got better?
lines.caption: When you change something, how do you know the results got better?

lines.text: The obvious way is to read every paper, every time.
lines.caption: The obvious way is to read every paper, every time.

lines.text: On this computer, just checking all 171 thousand papers for the two words takes about a tenth of a second.
lines.caption: On this computer, just checking all 171 thousand papers for the two words takes about a tenth of a second.

lines.text: But a web search engine covers hundreds of billions of pages.
lines.caption: But a web search engine covers hundreds of billions of pages.

lines.text: At this speed, even a billion papers like these would take over ten minutes, for one query.
lines.caption: At this speed, even a billion papers like these would take over ten minutes, for one query.

lines.text: So the work has to happen before anyone searches.
lines.caption: So the work has to happen before anyone searches.

lines.text: So, before any search, go through every paper once and flip it around: for every word, keep a list of the papers that contain it.
lines.caption: So, before any search, go through every paper once and flip it around: for every word, keep a list of the papers that contain it.

lines.text: That's an inverted index.
lines.caption: That's an inverted index.

lines.text: The list for one word is its posting list.
lines.caption: The list for one word is its posting list.

lines.text: Each entry, a posting, holds a paper's ID, how many times the word appears in it, and where.
lines.caption: Each entry, a posting, holds a paper's ID, how many times the word appears in it, and where.

lines.text: In this collection, the list for origin has 5,482 papers.
lines.caption: In this collection, the list for origin has 5,482 papers.

lines.text: The list for coronavirus has 35,095.
lines.caption: The list for coronavirus has 35,095.

lines.text: A query reads only the lists for its own words.
lines.caption: A query reads only the lists for its own words.

lines.text: The lists are sorted by paper ID, so you can walk two of them side by side and keep the papers on both: 1,644 have both words.
lines.caption: The lists are sorted by paper ID, so you can walk two of them side by side and keep the papers on both: 1,644 have both words.

lines.text: Or merge them, for papers with either word: 38,933.
lines.caption: Or merge them, for papers with either word: 38,933.

lines.text: Either way, the work grows with the length of those lists, not with the size of the collection.
lines.caption: Either way, the work grows with the length of those lists, not with the size of the collection.

lines.text: That's how the index answers in two milliseconds.
lines.caption: That's how the index answers in two milliseconds.

lines.text: But which strings count as the same word?
lines.caption: But which strings count as the same word?

lines.text: Origin, origins, Origin with a capital O?
lines.caption: Origin, origins, Origin with a capital O?

lines.text: Before anything goes into the index, an analyzer turns text into terms.
lines.caption: Before anything goes into the index, an analyzer turns text into terms.

lines.text: Here's the title of that top paper.
lines.caption: Here's the title of that top paper.

lines.text: The analyzer splits it into tokens, and lowercases them.
lines.caption: The analyzer splits it into tokens, and lowercases them.

lines.text: An English analyzer, like this one, also drops stop words, very common words like of and is.
lines.caption: An English analyzer, like this one, also drops stop words, very common words like of and is.

lines.text: And it stems: it cuts word endings off by rule, so origins becomes origin.
lines.caption: And it stems: it cuts word endings off by rule, so origins becomes origin.

lines.text: The stems don't have to be real words: coronavirus becomes corona vie roo.
lines.caption: The stems don't have to be real words: coronavirus becomes coronaviru.

lines.text: The query goes through the same analyzer, so its terms land on the same posting lists.
lines.caption: The query goes through the same analyzer, so its terms land on the same posting lists.

lines.text: Skip that step, and results vanish.
lines.caption: Skip that step, and results vanish.

lines.text: Look up Coronavirus exactly as typed, with its capital C, and the index has no such term: zero papers.
lines.caption: Look up Coronavirus exactly as typed, with its capital C, and the index has no such term: zero papers.

lines.text: Analyzing the index one way and the query another is a classic search bug.
lines.caption: Analyzing the index one way and the query another is a classic search bug.

lines.text: Now 38,933 papers contain at least one of the words.
lines.caption: Now 38,933 papers contain at least one of the words.

lines.text: Which ten go first?
lines.caption: Which ten go first?

lines.text: A classic answer is T F I D F.
lines.caption: A classic answer is TF-IDF.

lines.text: Term frequency: a paper that uses a word more is probably more about it.
lines.caption: Term frequency: a paper that uses a word more is probably more about it.

lines.text: Inverse document frequency: a rare word tells you more than a common one.
lines.caption: Inverse document frequency: a rare word tells you more than a common one.

lines.text: Origin is in about one paper in thirty-one, so its weight is the natural log of thirty-one: about 3.4.
lines.caption: Origin is in about one paper in thirty-one, so its weight is the natural log of thirty-one: about 3.4.

lines.text: Coronavirus is in about one in five, so it weighs 1.6.
lines.caption: Coronavirus is in about one in five, so it weighs 1.6.

lines.text: A paper's score is each word's count times its weight, added up.
lines.caption: A paper's score is each word's count times its weight, added up.

lines.text: Rank by that, and the top paper is about DNA replication origins.
lines.caption: Rank by that, and the top paper is about DNA replication origins.

lines.text: It says origin fourteen times, and never mentions a coronavirus.
lines.caption: It says origin fourteen times, and never mentions a coronavirus.

lines.text: Second is a paper twenty-five times the average length.
lines.caption: Second is a paper twenty-five times the average length.

lines.text: B M twenty-five fixes both problems.
lines.caption: BM25 fixes both problems.

lines.text: First, saturation: each extra mention adds less than the one before.
lines.caption: First, saturation: each extra mention adds less than the one before.

lines.text: A parameter called k one sets how fast the credit levels off; its default is 1.2.
lines.caption: A parameter called k1 sets how fast the credit levels off; its default is 1.2.

lines.text: Second, length normalization: a longer paper needs more mentions for the same credit.
lines.caption: Second, length normalization: a longer paper needs more mentions for the same credit.

lines.text: A parameter called b sets how much length counts; its default is 0.75.
lines.caption: A parameter called b sets how much length counts; its default is 0.75.

lines.text: With B M twenty-five, the top paper is about the origins of sars co vee two, the virus behind COVID-19.
lines.caption: With BM25, the top paper is about the origins of SARS-CoV-2, the virus behind COVID-19.

lines.text: It uses each word three times, in a shorter than average paper.
lines.caption: It uses each word three times, in a shorter than average paper.

lines.text: B M twenty-five comes from the 1990s, and it's still the default ranking in Loo-seen, the search library inside Elasticsearch.
lines.caption: BM25 comes from the 1990s, and it's still the default ranking in Lucene, the search library inside Elasticsearch.

lines.text: But B M twenty-five only counts words that match.
lines.caption: But BM25 only counts words that match.

lines.text: Take another topic in this collection: how long does coronavirus survive on surfaces.
lines.caption: Take another topic in this collection: how long does coronavirus survive on surfaces.

lines.text: Four of B M twenty-five's top ten are relevant; one of the others is about the surface of the eye.
lines.caption: Four of BM25's top ten are relevant; one of the others is about the surface of the eye.

lines.text: The relevant papers mostly say persistence, or stability, not survive.
lines.caption: The relevant papers mostly say persistence, or stability, not survive.

lines.text: That's the vocabulary mismatch problem: the same meaning, in different words.
lines.caption: That's the vocabulary mismatch problem: the same meaning, in different words.

lines.text: Dense retrieval matches meaning instead.
lines.caption: Dense retrieval matches meaning instead.

lines.text: An embedding model, a neural network trained on pairs of related texts, turns a text into a vector, here 384 numbers, so that texts with similar meanings point in similar directions.
lines.caption: An embedding model, a neural network trained on pairs of related texts, turns a text into a vector, here 384 numbers, so that texts with similar meanings point in similar directions.

lines.text: It encodes the query and each paper separately, so it's called a bi-encoder, and every paper's vector is computed once, in advance.
lines.caption: It encodes the query and each paper separately, so it's called a bi-encoder, and every paper's vector is computed once, in advance.

lines.text: Papers are ranked by cosine similarity: the cosine of the angle between their vector and the query's.
lines.caption: Papers are ranked by cosine similarity: the cosine of the angle between their vector and the query's.

lines.text: On the surfaces question, all ten of its top results are relevant.
lines.caption: On the surfaces question, all ten of its top results are relevant.

lines.text: But comparing the query with 171 thousand vectors is a scan again.
lines.caption: But comparing the query with 171 thousand vectors is a scan again.

lines.text: So vector search uses approximate nearest-neighbour search.
lines.caption: So vector search uses approximate nearest-neighbour search.

lines.text: A common method, H N S W, links each vector to a few near neighbours, in layers of graphs, and hops greedily toward the query.
lines.caption: A common method, HNSW, links each vector to a few near neighbours, in layers of graphs, and hops greedily toward the query.

lines.text: Here it compared about twelve hundred vectors, not 171 thousand, and still found about ninety-nine percent of the true top ten.
lines.caption: Here it compared about twelve hundred vectors, not 171 thousand, and still found about ninety-nine percent of the true top ten.

lines.text: Approximate means it can miss a few.
lines.caption: Approximate means it can miss a few.

lines.text: Dense retrieval has its own blind spot: exact names and codes.
lines.caption: Dense retrieval has its own blind spot: exact names and codes.

lines.text: Search for D614G, the name of a mutation in the virus.
lines.caption: Search for D614G, the name of a mutation in the virus.

lines.text: All of B M twenty-five's top ten contain it.
lines.caption: All of BM25's top ten contain it.

lines.text: Only one of dense retrieval's does; the rest are mostly lists of conference posters, with codes like P441.
lines.caption: Only one of dense retrieval's does; the rest are mostly lists of conference posters, with codes like P441.

lines.text: So run both, and merge the two rankings.
lines.caption: So run both, and merge the two rankings.

lines.text: That's hybrid search.
lines.caption: That's hybrid search.

lines.text: Their scores aren't on the same scale, so merge by rank.
lines.caption: Their scores aren't on the same scale, so merge by rank.

lines.text: Reciprocal rank fusion gives a paper one over sixty plus its rank, from each ranking, and adds them up.
lines.caption: Reciprocal rank fusion gives a paper one over sixty plus its rank, from each ranking, and adds them up.

lines.text: Both still score the query and each paper separately.
lines.caption: Both still score the query and each paper separately.

lines.text: A cross-encoder reads them together, as one input, so every word of the query can be weighed against every word of the paper.
lines.caption: A cross-encoder reads them together, as one input, so every word of the query can be weighed against every word of the paper.

lines.text: It ranks better, but it's slow: on this computer, about thirty-five papers a second.
lines.caption: It ranks better, but it's slow: on this computer, about thirty-five papers a second.

lines.text: The whole collection would take over an hour, for one query.
lines.caption: The whole collection would take over an hour, for one query.

lines.text: So search is built as a funnel.
lines.caption: So search is built as a funnel.

lines.text: Cheap retrieval over the whole collection picks the candidates, in milliseconds.
lines.caption: Cheap retrieval over the whole collection picks the candidates, in milliseconds.

lines.text: The expensive reranker orders only the top hundred.
lines.caption: The expensive reranker orders only the top hundred.

lines.text: Rerankers can also learn to weigh other signals, like freshness and past clicks: that's learning to rank.
lines.caption: Rerankers can also learn to weigh other signals, like freshness and past clicks: that's learning to rank.

lines.text: So each stage has its own job.
lines.caption: So each stage has its own job.

lines.text: Retrieval must not lose the good papers.
lines.caption: Retrieval must not lose the good papers.

lines.text: Reranking must put the best of them on top.
lines.caption: Reranking must put the best of them on top.

lines.text: Every step so far was supposed to make the results better.
lines.caption: Every step so far was supposed to make the results better.

lines.text: How do you check?
lines.caption: How do you check?

lines.text: You need to know which papers are actually relevant, and that takes people.
lines.caption: You need to know which papers are actually relevant, and that takes people.

lines.text: A test collection has three parts: the papers, a set of topics, each a query with a description of what the searcher wants, and relevance judgments, often called Q rels.
lines.caption: A test collection has three parts: the papers, a set of topics, each a query with a description of what the searcher wants, and relevance judgments, often called qrels.

lines.text: This collection comes from Treck Covid, a 2020 evaluation run by the US National Institute of Standards and Technology.
lines.caption: This collection comes from TREC-COVID, a 2020 evaluation run by the US National Institute of Standards and Technology.

lines.text: Judging every paper for each of fifty topics would take eight and a half million judgments.
lines.caption: Judging every paper for each of fifty topics would take eight and a half million judgments.

lines.text: So Treck uses pooling.
lines.caption: So TREC uses pooling.

lines.text: Dozens of teams submitted rankings, the top papers from those rankings were pooled, and people with medical expertise judged each one: relevant, partially relevant, or not relevant.
lines.caption: Dozens of teams submitted rankings, the top papers from those rankings were pooled, and people with medical expertise judged each one: relevant, partially relevant, or not relevant.

lines.text: About sixty-six thousand judgments in all.
lines.caption: About sixty-six thousand judgments in all.

lines.text: A paper nobody judged counts as not relevant.
lines.caption: A paper nobody judged counts as not relevant.

lines.text: That's pooling's known weakness: a new system that finds different papers can be scored too low.
lines.caption: That's pooling's known weakness: a new system that finds different papers can be scored too low.

lines.text: With judgments, you can score any list of results.
lines.caption: With judgments, you can score any list of results.

lines.text: Precision: of the papers returned, the fraction that are relevant.
lines.caption: Precision: of the papers returned, the fraction that are relevant.

lines.text: Recall: of all the relevant papers, the fraction that were returned.
lines.caption: Recall: of all the relevant papers, the fraction that were returned.

lines.text: They pull against each other.
lines.caption: They pull against each other.

lines.text: For coronavirus origin, 637 papers are judged relevant.
lines.caption: For coronavirus origin, 637 papers are judged relevant.

lines.text: B M twenty-five's top ten has nine of them: precision 0.9, but recall only 1.4 percent.
lines.caption: BM25's top ten has nine of them: precision 0.9, but recall only 1.4 percent.

lines.text: Its top thousand finds 255: recall 40 percent, but precision down to about a quarter.
lines.caption: Its top thousand finds 255: recall 40 percent, but precision down to about a quarter.

lines.text: Return more, and recall can only rise, while precision usually falls.
lines.caption: Return more, and recall can only rise, while precision usually falls.

lines.text: A ranked list is read from the top, so measure it at a cutoff.
lines.caption: A ranked list is read from the top, so measure it at a cutoff.

lines.text: Precision at ten counts the relevant papers in the top ten: what people actually see.
lines.caption: Precision at ten counts the relevant papers in the top ten: what people actually see.

lines.text: Recall at a hundred asks what share of all the relevant papers made the top hundred: what a reranker gets to see.
lines.caption: Recall at a hundred asks what share of all the relevant papers made the top hundred: what a reranker gets to see.

lines.text: Precision at ten ignores order: a relevant paper counts the same in first place as in tenth.
lines.caption: Precision at ten ignores order: a relevant paper counts the same in first place as in tenth.

lines.text: Two measures care about order.
lines.caption: Two measures care about order.

lines.text: Reciprocal rank is one over the rank of the first relevant result: one if it's first, a half if it's second.
lines.caption: Reciprocal rank is one over the rank of the first relevant result: one if it's first, a half if it's second.

lines.text: Its average over all the topics is the mean reciprocal rank, M R R.
lines.caption: Its average over all the topics is the mean reciprocal rank, MRR.

lines.text: It suits searches with one right answer.
lines.caption: It suits searches with one right answer.

lines.text: N D C G also uses the grades.
lines.caption: NDCG also uses the grades.

lines.text: Each paper's gain is its grade: two for relevant, one for partially relevant.
lines.caption: Each paper's gain is its grade: two for relevant, one for partially relevant.

lines.text: Divide each gain by a discount that grows with the rank, the log base two of the rank plus one, and add them up.
lines.caption: Divide each gain by a discount that grows with the rank, the log base two of the rank plus one, and add them up.

lines.text: That's the discounted cumulative gain, or D C G.
lines.caption: That's the discounted cumulative gain, or DCG.

lines.text: For B M twenty-five's top ten, it's 7.06.
lines.caption: For BM25's top ten, it's 7.06.

lines.text: The best possible top ten, ten papers graded two, would score 9.09.
lines.caption: The best possible top ten, ten papers graded two, would score 9.09.

lines.text: Divide one by the other, and you get normalized D C G, N D C G at ten: 0.78, where one is perfect.
lines.caption: Divide one by the other, and you get normalized DCG, NDCG at ten: 0.78, where one is perfect.

lines.text: Now score every stage over all fifty topics.
lines.caption: Now score every stage over all fifty topics.

lines.text: Here each topic's full question is the query, the standard setup for this collection.
lines.caption: Here each topic's full question is the query, the standard setup for this collection.

lines.text: B M twenty-five doubles T F I D F's N D C G at ten, from 0.30 to 0.61.
lines.caption: BM25 doubles TF-IDF's NDCG at ten, from 0.30 to 0.61.

lines.text: Dense retrieval alone scores 0.47, below B M twenty-five, though four in ten of its top papers were never judged.
lines.caption: Dense retrieval alone scores 0.47, below BM25, though four in ten of its top papers were never judged.

lines.text: Hybrid search beats both, at 0.68.
lines.caption: Hybrid search beats both, at 0.68.

lines.text: And reranking its top hundred lifts it to 0.74.
lines.caption: And reranking its top hundred lifts it to 0.74.

lines.text: Recall at a hundred doesn't move, because the reranker only reorders.
lines.caption: Recall at a hundred doesn't move, because the reranker only reorders.

lines.text: M R R barely moves either: with hundreds of relevant papers per topic, almost any decent ranking starts with one.
lines.caption: MRR barely moves either: with hundreds of relevant papers per topic, almost any decent ranking starts with one.

lines.text: Those are offline numbers: fixed judgments, repeatable, and cheap to rerun after every change.
lines.caption: Those are offline numbers: fixed judgments, repeatable, and cheap to rerun after every change.

lines.text: But judges aren't your users.
lines.caption: But judges aren't your users.

lines.text: Online evaluation shows a change to a random share of real users, an A B test, and compares what they do: what they click, how often they rephrase, how often they give up.
lines.caption: Online evaluation shows a change to a random share of real users, an A/B test, and compares what they do: what they click, how often they rephrase, how often they give up.

lines.text: Clicks are biased, though.
lines.caption: Clicks are biased, though.

lines.text: In one eye-tracking study, when the top two results were swapped, people still clicked the first one more, even when the second was more relevant.
lines.caption: In one eye-tracking study, when the top two results were swapped, people still clicked the first one more, even when the second was more relevant.

lines.text: And a change that wins offline can still lose with users.
lines.caption: And a change that wins offline can still lose with users.

lines.text: So teams use both: offline tests to choose what's worth trying, online tests to decide what ships.
lines.caption: So teams use both: offline tests to choose what's worth trying, online tests to decide what ships.

lines.text: So how do ten good papers come back from 171 thousand, in two milliseconds?
lines.caption: So how do ten good papers come back from 171 thousand, in two milliseconds?

lines.text: Before any search, an analyzer turns every paper into terms, and an inverted index lists the papers for each term.
lines.caption: Before any search, an analyzer turns every paper into terms, and an inverted index lists the papers for each term.

lines.text: A query reads a few posting lists, never the whole collection, and B M twenty-five ranks the matches.
lines.caption: A query reads a few posting lists, never the whole collection, and BM25 ranks the matches.

lines.text: To do better, add stages: vectors for the same meaning in other words, and a reranker for the top hundred, each costing more time.
lines.caption: To do better, add stages: vectors for the same meaning in other words, and a reranker for the top hundred, each costing more time.

lines.text: And relevance judgments, with measures like N D C G, tell you in numbers whether a change helped.
lines.caption: And relevance judgments, with measures like NDCG, tell you in numbers whether a change helped.

lines.text: Nine of that first top ten were relevant.
lines.caption: Nine of that first top ten were relevant.

lines.text: The same pipeline now feeds language models.
lines.caption: The same pipeline now feeds language models.

lines.text: Retrieval-augmented generation searches first, and puts what it finds into the model's context.
lines.caption: Retrieval-augmented generation searches first, and puts what it finds into the model's context.
